location: Methods - Cumulative EUD and recovery; Table 3 'Corrected sum'
organ: CNS (optic chiasm, optic nerves, brainstem, brain)
setting: Recurrent malignant glioma re-irradiation; interval generally >6 months
intervalRule: Uniform empiric recovery factor r = 0.5 applied to the primary-course dose regardless of interval (descriptive analysis, not a validated planning rule)
quote: an empiric recovery factor of r = 0.5 for the primary radiation dose was introduced which should account for repair of normal CNS tissue; this uniform value was rather an approximation and simplification
notes: Applied to EUD and maximum dose values (Gy), not to EQD2/BED explicitly. intervalMonthsMin is null because the factor was applied irrespective of interval (cohort interval >= 5.8 months). Authors state optic system and other CNS tissues likely differ in recovery.

location: Section 'Normal tissue tolerance' (citing Ang et al. 2001, rhesus monkey spinal cord)
setting: Experimental primate spinal cord data, cited in brain reirradiation review
intervalRule: estimated recovery of occult injury after a first course of RT around 50% at 1 year, 60% at 2 years, and 65–70% at 3 years or more
quote: the authors suggested to use an estimated recovery of occult injury after a first course of RT around 50% at 1 year, 60% at 2 years, and 65–70% at 3 years or more, for the reirradiation of selected patients
notes: retainedFraction DERIVED as 1 - stated recovery; for >=3 years the conservative end (65% recovery -> 0.35 retained) is used, the stated range is 65-70%. Source data are spinal cord (secondary citation of Ang 2001); the review states brain recovery is 'assumed to be like' spinal cord. Interval bins between the stated time points are my interpretation (value at 1 y applied from 12-24 months, etc.) - treat with caution; no value given for <12 months.

intervalRule: No correlation between interval (3-55 months) and re-irradiation tolerance; authors suggest relatively fast partial long-term recovery (months rather than years). No quantitative factors.
quote: These observations suggest a relatively fast process of (partial) long-term recovery, in the order of months rather than of years.

intervalRule: Reirradiation should be considered at least 6 months after the first course of RT (glioblastoma); optic nerves/chiasm have limited recovery regardless of interval. No retained-dose factors.
quote: According to international recommendations and prognostic scores for glioblastoma patients, reirradiation should be considered at least 6 months after the first course of RT [6].
notes: Patient-selection interval, not a dose-discount model.
